program_name: Wildlife Management, Conservation and Control (WMCC) — International Master's Degree. The university-level catalogue lists the title as 'WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, CONSERVATION, AND CONTROL' (internal course code A193 / degree id 6250); the Department of Veterinary Medicine and all official course documents use the acronym WMCC.
level: master (Laurea Magistrale, second-cycle degree, 2 years, 120 ECTS; final degree awarded out of 110, requires 197 ECTS accumulated to be admitted to the final examination per the 2025/2026 Manifesto)
teaching_language: English — fully English-taught, with no Italian-language curriculum or alternative track. The Manifesto of Studies states 'Official language of the course is English' and the university-level page lists 'Course language: English'. English proficiency at CEFR B2 is a substantive admission condition, not merely a formality. A dedicated 6-ECTS 'English Language (Advanced)' course (SSD L-LIN/12, 16 lecture + 50 practical hours) is embedded in Year 1 Semester I to harmonise students' linguistic skills. No partial-English or bilingual sub-curriculum exists for this programme.
campus: Sassari — Campus of the Department of Veterinary Medicine, Via Vienna 2, 07100 Sassari, Sardinia, Italy. This is the main Sassari campus, NOT one of UNISS's satellite campuses (Alghero, Olbia, Nuoro, Oristano). Both the department page ('campus of Veterinary Medicine, Via Vienna 2, Sassari, Sardinia, Italy') and the university-level page ('SASSARI') confirm this. Teaching includes compulsory in-person laboratory and outdoor fieldwork, so physical presence in Sassari is required despite the mostly online admission process.
degree_class: LM-86 — 'Scienze zootecniche e tecnologie animali' (Zootechnical Sciences and Animal Technologies). The university catalogue displays the reformed class code '[LM-86-R]'; the 2025/2026 Manifesto of Studies heads the document 'MASTER'S DEGREE IN WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT, CONSERVATION AND CONTROL (LM-86)'. LM-86 and LM-86-R refer to the same class (the -R suffix marks the post-DM 1649/2023 reformed class ordinance).
admission_type: Open access (Italian 'accesso libero' / 'Type of access: Free') with a MANDATORY entry test — but with a hidden non-EU seat cap. Three layers must be understood together: (1) There is no numerus clausus and no overall cap on admitted students; the university-level page states 'Tipologia di accesso: Libero' ('Type of access: Free') and the Manifesto states 'Access: Open'. (2) HOWEVER, the department page discloses a quota that does NOT appear anywhere on the university-level uniss.it page: 'Number of admitted students: no overall limitation (max 15 non-EU students)'. Non-EU applicants therefore compete for a maximum of 15 places per intake — this is the single most important constraint for international applicants and it is only findable on veterinaria.uniss.it. (3) Admission is nevertheless not automatic: it is gated by (a) a documentary eligibility check performed by the secretary's office on degree class and ECTS content, and (b) participation in a compulsory entry test whose English interview component is the actual determinant. Formally the enrolment page describes it as 'a free access course', and the required steps are: meet the degree/ECTS requirements, hold English B2, and 'have participated in the entry test'. So: open access in the Italian administrative sense, but with a documentary pre-check, a compulsory (partly diagnostic) test, and a hard 15-place ceiling for non-EU candidates.
academic_requirements: ACCEPTED DEGREES (either route). Route A — a first-level (Bachelor) degree recognised at European level, or an equivalent title, in one of: Biology, Natural Sciences, Environmental Sciences, Forestry, Animal Breeding, or Veterinary Medicine. Route B — a DIFFERENT first-level (Bachelor) degree, provided the academic background includes a MINIMUM OF 36 ECTS CREDITS in the following core disciplines: anatomy, physiology, microbiology, parasitology, zoology, ecology, and genetics. For Italian students these are identified by the Italian scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD): VET/01, VET/02, VET/05, VET/06, BIO/05, BIO/07, BIO/18, AGR/07, AGR/16. The 36 ECTS is a cumulative total across those disciplines, not a per-discipline minimum. DOCUMENTARY EVALUATION: 'Students are requested to provide a documentation proving the fulfilment of the abovementioned requirements. The secretary office will evaluate the documentation and a feedback will be given on the possible admission to the Master's Course.' For non-EU applicants this pre-check is an explicit first step performed by email to wmcc@uniss.it, and positive feedback is required BEFORE the applicant may register on Universitaly. The enrolment page adds that for holders of a non-listed bachelor's degree the sufficiency of the background is 'assessed by the evaluation of the transcripts of records'. CONDITIONAL / INCOMPLETE DEGREE: candidates who have not yet completed the bachelor's degree or the required credits may be temporarily admitted — 'Students have time to achieve the above mentioned title/credits by December 31st, and in the meantime they can temporarily be admitted and proceed with a conditional registration to the Master's Course. In any case, the enrolment procedure must be completed by mid January.' NON-EU SEAT CAP: a maximum of 15 non-EU students may be admitted per intake ('no overall limitation (max 15 non-EU students)'). This cap is published ONLY on the Department of Veterinary Medicine pages (veterinaria.uniss.it) and is absent from the university-level uniss.it course page, which advertises only 'accesso libero'. ENGLISH AS AN ACADEMIC REQUIREMENT: 'Admission is conditional upon possession of a B2 level of knowledge of the English language.' ENTRY TEST FORMAT (see entry_exam_or_test for full detail): a 25-question multiple-choice academic test that is explicitly NON-BINDING for admission ('The multiple choice test does not affect the student's admission but is only aimed at assessing the initial preparation' / 'The test result is not binding for admission purposes; it is designed to ascertain students' initial knowledge'), plus an English-language interview that also probes previous experience and motivation and is the component that actually determines admission. NOTE: attendance at lectures is not compulsory ('Attendance at lectures and practical activities is not compulsory'), although the key-information box describes the study mode as 'compulsory lectures and practical activities' — a contradiction between the department summary box and the Manifesto.
language_requirements: CEFR B2 in English is the minimum and is a condition of admission: 'Admission is conditional upon possession of a B2 level of knowledge of the English language.' THREE ALTERNATIVE WAYS TO SATISFY IT, all officially accepted and treated as equivalent: (1) assessment during the entry-test interview — the department page states 'English level B2 (assessed during the entry test)' and the Manifesto 'English level B2 (certificated or assessed during the entry test)'; the interview is 'aimed at evaluating the knowledge of English language' and to 'assess English language interaction skills'; (2) a CEFR certificate — 'submitting a corresponding (Common European Framework of Reference for languages - CEFR) certificate'; (3) prior university examinations — 'The English level B2 (or higher) can be also proven by having passed university examinations of equivalent level.' NO FIXED SCORE TABLE IS PUBLISHED. UNISS/WMCC does NOT publish a list of accepted certificates or minimum IELTS/TOEFL/Cambridge/Duolingo scores anywhere on the official pages; the only stated standard is the CEFR B2 level itself. This means a candidate without a certificate is NOT excluded — the interview route is a genuine, officially sanctioned alternative. Non-EU applicants are asked to send an English certificate with the preliminary documentation only 'if you have it' ('Also, if you have it, please send a certificate of knowledge of the English language'), confirming it is optional rather than mandatory. No Italian-language requirement exists for admission or graduation.
application_deadline_eu: AY 2026/2027 — FOUR entry-test rounds, each with its own registration window (these ARE the effective application deadlines; there is no single annual application deadline). Official 'Entry Test schedule, Academic Year 2026/2027': (1) Test 2026-02-25 — registration window 2026-01-21 to 2026-02-20; (2) Test 2026-04-15 — registration window 2026-02-21 to 2026-04-10; (3) Test 2026-07-09 — registration window 2026-04-11 to 2026-07-04; (4) Test 2026-09-15 — registration window 2026-07-05 to 2026-09-10. Registration for a test round is done on the Self Studenti Uniss portal (uniss.esse3.cineca.it) after creating an account; a step-by-step tutorial is published. FOUR-STEP EU PROCEDURE: '1) ONLINE REGISTRATION: register on the portal Self Studenti Uniss; 2) PRE-ENROLMENT: pre-enrol online in the portal Self Studenti Uniss; 3) ENTRY TEST: participate in the entry test; 4) ENROLMENT: after the entry test, once formally admitted, the student has to fulfil the online application.' Fees are paid via PagoPA. CONDITIONAL-ENROLMENT RULE (applies to EU candidates who have not yet graduated): the bachelor's degree and/or the required credits may be obtained up to 31 December, with temporary/conditional registration in the meantime, but 'the enrolment procedure must be completed by mid January' (the parallel non-EU document fixes this as 15 January). CLASSES START at the beginning of October. NOTE: the four dates above are the 2026/2027 schedule as published by the department; the 2025/2026 schedule had a comparable four-round shape (10 April 2025, 2 July 2025, 10 September 2025, 30 October 2025), so an additional late-October round for 2026/2027 cannot be ruled out but is not currently published.
application_deadline_non_eu: AY 2026/2027 — the SAME four entry-test rounds and registration windows as EU candidates (test 2026-02-25, reg. 2026-01-21 to 2026-02-20; test 2026-04-15, reg. 2026-02-21 to 2026-04-10; test 2026-07-09, reg. 2026-04-11 to 2026-07-04; test 2026-09-15, reg. 2026-07-05 to 2026-09-10), PLUS three extra non-EU-only stages and their own deadlines. FIVE-STEP NON-EU PROCEDURE: '1. Sending preliminary documentation to UNISS and wait for its evaluation; 2. Entry test for admission to WMCC; 3. Registration on Universitaly portal for pre-enrolment; 4. Application for an entry visa to the Italian embassy through Universitaly; 5. Enrolment to WMCC.' (a) PRELIMINARY DOCUMENT CHECK — documents are emailed to wmcc@uniss.it and must be positively assessed BEFORE Universitaly registration; no fixed deadline is published for this step, so candidates should start well ahead of their chosen test round. (b) UNIVERSITALY PRE-ENROLMENT — a separate, mandatory visa pre-enrolment step on universitaly.it, done only 'Once the university staff has checked your documentation and you have received positive feedback on admittance'; a passport must be uploaded. (c) STUDY VISA — 'The procedures for issuing this visa must be concluded by the Embassy/Consulate, without prejudice to possible different future instruction, by 30 November.' Visa procedures and deadlines follow the annual MUR/MAECI/Interior Ministry directives and vary by consulate; it is the candidate's responsibility to check local procedures. (d) FINAL ENROLMENT WINDOW — 'you can enrol to the University of Sassari through the portal Self Studenti Uniss starting from 1 August (until 15 January)', i.e. enrolment opens 2026-08-01 and closes 2026-01-15 (for the 2026/2027 intake). This 15 January date is the concrete expression of the 'mid January' deadline in the Manifesto. CONDITIONAL ENROLMENT applies identically: degree/credits by 31 December, enrolment completed by 15 January. SEAT CAP: only 15 non-EU students may be admitted, so earlier rounds are materially safer than the September round. IMPORTANT WARNING published by the department: 'The preliminary acceptance by the University does not confer any right to obtain a visa and it does not imply any right to the subsequent enrolment.' CLASSES START at the beginning of October — note the tension between an October start, a 30 November visa deadline and a 15 January enrolment deadline, which exists precisely to accommodate late visa issuance.
required_documents: FOR THE PRELIMINARY ELIGIBILITY CHECK (non-EU applicants, emailed to wmcc@uniss.it — and in substance the same evidence any applicant must supply to the secretary's office): 'you must send: the identity document, the CV, the Secondary School Certificate, the First Degree Level (Bachelor) Certificate, Academic Transcript of Records of the First Degree. Also, if you have it, please send a certificate of knowledge of the English language.' So: (1) identity document / passport; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) secondary school (high school) certificate; (4) bachelor's degree certificate; (5) academic transcript of records of the bachelor's degree — this is the document used to verify the 36-ECTS core-discipline requirement for non-listed degrees; (6) English language certificate — OPTIONAL ('if you have it'), since B2 can instead be assessed at the interview. FOR THE ENTRY-TEST REGISTRATION on Self Studenti Uniss: an identity document must be uploaded as part of the online pre-enrolment steps. FOR UNIVERSITALY PRE-ENROLMENT (non-EU only): personal and academic details plus supporting documents, 'such as your passport. Each document must be uploaded as a single item'; a confirmation email follows. The department advises 'Keep copies of all documents you submit, as you may need them for your visa or residence permit application' and 'Keeping a copy of the pre-enrolment form is highly advisable.' NOT REQUIRED: no motivation letter, reference letters, research proposal, portfolio or application fee are listed as separate documents — motivation is instead probed orally in the interview. Standard Italian legalisation items (Declaration of Value / CIMEA statement of comparability, translated and legalised diplomas) are not itemised on the WMCC pages but are normally requested by the consulate at the visa stage.
entry_exam_or_test: YES — a compulsory two-part entry test, but ONLY ONE PART ACTUALLY GATES ADMISSION. PART 1 — WRITTEN MULTIPLE-CHOICE TEST, 25 questions across five subject blocks: Anatomy and Physiology (5 questions), Microbiology (5), Vertebrate Zoology (5), Animal Ecology (5), Genetics (5). This part is EXPLICITLY DIAGNOSTIC AND NON-BINDING — it does NOT affect admission. The department states it twice, unambiguously: 'The test result is not binding for admission purposes; it is designed to ascertain students' initial knowledge' and 'The multiple choice test does not affect the student's admission but is only aimed at assessing the initial preparation.' There is no pass mark, no threshold score and no ranking derived from it; its purpose is to let the course identify knowledge gaps in the incoming cohort. Candidates should therefore not treat it as a competitive exam. PART 2 — INTERVIEW, conducted in English. This is the component that actually determines admission. Its stated purposes are 'to ascertain previous experience and motivation to participate in the course, and to assess English language interaction skills', and it is 'aimed at evaluating the knowledge of English language and degree of motivation to attend the course'. Since admission 'is conditional upon possession of a B2 level of knowledge of the English language' and B2 may be evidenced by the interview itself, the interview is the operative gate: a candidate whose English is judged below B2 (and who holds no equivalent certificate or university examination) fails the admission condition regardless of the multiple-choice score. MODALITY: the test is held online. The official WMCC 'how to enroll' page for the 2024/2025 intake stated 'participate in the entry test that will be held online on 16/9/2024 at 9.30 a.m.' with 'an interview (in English)'. The 2026/2027 schedule PDF does not restate the platform or start time, so the exact conferencing tool and time for each 2026/2027 round should be confirmed with wmcc@uniss.it. REGISTRATION: candidates must first create an account on Self Studenti Uniss (uniss.esse3.cineca.it), then pre-enrol for a specific test session via Registrar's Office > start registration > course type > test type > confirm > upload identity document; a step-by-step tutorial PDF is published by the department. ALL 2026/2027 SESSIONS (four rounds, each with its own registration window): 25 February 2026 (register 21 January – 20 February 2026); 15 April 2026 (register 21 February – 10 April 2026); 9 July 2026 (register 11 April – 4 July 2026); 15 September 2026 (register 5 July – 10 September 2026). For comparison, the 2025/2026 rounds were 10 April 2025, 2 July 2025, 10 September 2025 and 30 October 2025. There is no separate written admission exam beyond this test, and no TOLC, SAT, GRE or GMAT requirement of any kind.
tuition_or_fees_link: https://www.uniss.it/en/teaching/student-services/guide-studenti/tuition-fees-and-isee — SUMMARY: the WMCC department page states 'the amount of tuition varies according to economic status, study merit and country of origin (from 0 up to a maximum of around 1,800 € per year (plus around 150 € of regional taxes)'. So the realistic range is EUR 0 to about EUR 1,800 per year plus roughly EUR 150 of regional (ERSU) tax. STRUCTURE: enrolment is subject to a single enrolment fee (contributo onnicomprensivo) + a virtual stamp duty of EUR 16.00 + the regional ERSU tax, with the single fee calculated from the family ISEE indicator and paid in three instalments (first instalment up to EUR 310.00 with the EUR 16.00 stamp duty, then a second and a possible balancing third instalment). KEY RULE FOR INTERNATIONAL STUDENTS: 'Foreign students residing abroad are fully exempt from paying the single registration fee for the first year of enrollment.' For years after the first (within the normal course duration) foreign students residing abroad pay a flat fee based on their country's GDP per capita (PPP) bracket as calculated by the IMF: Bracket 1 EUR 700.00, Bracket 2 EUR 500.00, Bracket 3 EUR 400.00, Bracket 4 EUR 300.00; they may alternatively submit an ISEE if it is more favourable. OTHER EXEMPTIONS: students with an ISEE at or below EUR 22,000 who meet the merit requirements are exempt from the single enrolment fee under Law 232/2016 (the Italian 'no-tax area'); ERSU regional scholarship holders and eligible non-beneficiaries are exempt from the single fee; holders of Italian Government (MAECI) scholarships under cooperation and cultural/scientific agreements are fully exempt. Exempt students still owe the virtual stamp duty and, where due, the ERSU regional tax. SCHOLARSHIPS: UNISS itself does not advertise a dedicated WMCC scholarship on the current pages; international students are directed to the regional ERSU Sassari scholarship and housing call and to MAECI Italian Government scholarships. (Historically the department published a 'bando borse di studio' specifically for the WMCC master's degree, so it is worth asking wmcc@uniss.it whether a course-specific scholarship call is open.) Mobility grants (Erasmus+, Ulisse) are available to enrolled students by public selection.

uncertainty_notes: ACADEMIC YEAR OF THE DATA. Admission dates are 2026/2027 and are firm: the department published a dedicated 'Entry Test schedule — Academic Year 2026/2027' PDF (file path dated 2026-01) listing all four rounds. However, the substantive ACADEMIC and LANGUAGE requirements, the fee range and the programme structure are taken from the Manifesto of Studies 2025/2026, because a 2026/2027 Manifesto has NOT yet been published — as of a live check on 2026-09-05 the department page still links only 'Manifesto degli studi 2025-26', and the university-level page's 'Vedi anche' link is even older ('LM86WL manifesto 24-25'). Requirements have been stable across recent years, but the 36-ECTS threshold, the accepted degree list and the SSD codes should be re-verified against the 2026/2027 Manifesto once it appears. ACCESS METHOD TO SOURCES. uniss.it and veterinaria.uniss.it are behind bot protection that returns HTTP 405 to direct automated requests; every page and PDF cited here was therefore read through Internet Archive Wayback Machine captures of the official URLs. The three 2026-01 PDFs (entry tests 2026/2027, EU procedure, non-EU procedure) and the current department page were archived on demand on 2026-09-05, so they reflect the LIVE content as of that date; the fees page and the older 'how to enroll' page are from earlier captures. No third-party aggregator was used. [uncertain] ENTRY TEST MODALITY AND TIME. That the test is held ONLINE is stated explicitly only on the older official WMCC 'how to enroll' page for the 2024/2025 intake ('held online on 16/9/2024 at 9.30 a.m.'). The 2026/2027 schedule PDF gives dates but names neither the platform (Teams/Zoom/other) nor the start time, and the current pages do not restate the modality. Online delivery is very likely to continue but the platform and per-round start time must be confirmed with wmcc@uniss.it. [uncertain] EXACT EU FINAL-ENROLMENT DATE. The Manifesto and department page say only 'the enrolment procedure must be completed by mid January'; the concrete date 15 January is stated in the NON-EU procedure PDF. The EU procedure PDF gives no closing date at all, so 15 January is inferred for EU candidates and should be confirmed. [uncertain] NUMBER OF ROUNDS. The 2025/2026 calendar had a fourth, late-October round (30 October 2025) that fell after the start of classes; the published 2026/2027 calendar ends on 15 September 2026. Nonetheless, students are warmly encouraged to attend all teaching activities.' The Manifesto is the governing regulation and should be preferred. STRUCTURAL WARNING FOR NON-EU APPLICANTS. The 15-place non-EU cap is published ONLY on veterinaria.uniss.it and appears nowhere on the uniss.it course page, which advertises the programme as freely accessible; the official pages do not explain how candidates are ranked or selected if more than 15 eligible non-EU applicants apply, nor whether the cap is allocated per test round or across the whole year. Given that, and the 30 November visa deadline, non-EU candidates should target one of the earlier rounds (February or April 2026) rather than the September round.
